topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture begins with opening framing that outlines the learning objectives and conceptual framework for understanding cancer evolution and the microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal Selection and Darwinian Evolution in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic presents experimental evidence demonstrating that tumors develop through Darwinian selection and clonal expansion of cells carrying advantageous driver mutations.

topics.label: Epigenetic Regulation in Tumor Formation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how transient alterations in the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape can drive tumor development independently of genetic mutations.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Hierarchical Models of Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how normal tissue stem cell hierarchies and cell-of-origin properties influence susceptibility to oncogenic transformation and tumor propagation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Promotion and Chronic Inflammation in Cancer Growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how extrinsic microenvironmental stimuli, chronic inflammation, and supportive stroma act alongside mutations to promote malignant initiation and maintain tumor growth.

topics.label: Methods for Investigating Cancer Evolution and the Microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes experimental and computational methods, such as single-cell sequencing and spatial omics, used to analyse mutational timing and tumor-microenvironment interactions.

topics.label: Synthesis of Multi-Factorial Cancer Evolution and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the combined contributions of genetic, epigenetic, cell-of-origin, and microenvironmental factors to cancer evolution before concluding the lecture.
